question:
For each of the following, given a sample is being taken from the Large Data Set, write down the name of the sampling method used.

  1. The order of the cars is randomised, then every 100th is noted.

  2. The order of the cars is randomised, then the first 10 of each type of make is noted to obtain 50 cars.

  3. The data set is sorted by makes and the proportions of each type calculated. Using a random number generator and the reference number, each make is selected to the same proportion as the full data set.

Martha uses the complete Large Data Set and finds that the mean mass of a car in 2002 is 1278.7 kg and in 2016 is 1416.6 kg. She finds out that the average mass of a human in 2002 and 2016 was 75.9 kg and 78.0 kg respectively.

  1. She says the actual mass of the cars is 1202.8 kg and 1338.6 kg. Explain why Martha is incorrect.

  2. She claims that all vehicles in the UK are heavier in 2016 than in 2002. Comment on the validity of Martha's claim.
steps:
a)

Incorrect as 75kg is included in the mass, not the mean mass of the population at the time

b)

Incorrect as the LDS doesn’t include: All car manufacturers All regions of the UK Vehicles other than cars

question:
A set of 100 cars were sampled from the Large Data Set and the engine sizes of these cars are displayed in the boxplot below:

Using your knowledge of the Large Data Set, explain why it is possible that it was not sampled randomly.
steps: Engine sizes vary between 647 and 4951 so the data lies within this, but the middle 50% of the Large Data Set lies between 1395 and 1968. The box plot has a much lower middle 50% so it is likely that there has been a higher selection of lower engines selected which indicates it may not have been sampled randomly.
